blindSummary:
The situation here for transgender visitors is legally unremarkable and socially mixed. Same-sex conduct is legal; the constitution's "any other status" equality clause is read to cover SOGI discrimination; and a 2022 equal-treatment labour act added employment protections. There is no legal gender recognition and no documented trans-murder pattern, but the small LGBT community in the capital reports routine harassment, and the interior offers essentially no protection.

For a visitor: no legal exposure; modest street risk in the capital; low tourist infrastructure generally.
blindOutOfScope: The absence of legal gender recognition and the governance gaps in the interior are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the constitution's equality clause prohibits discrimination including 'any other status' (argued to extend to SOGI); the 2022 equal-treatment labour act explicitly bans SOGI discrimination at work; same-sex intercourse not criminalised; the penal code protects against hate speech; legal gender recognition advanced via a January 2022 appeals-court ruling ordering civil-registration changes for a trans woman.

Civil-society report (a local health foundation, an AIDS-service NGO and the national LGBT platform) to a UN human-rights treaty body's 141st session (July 2024) on ICCPR implementation in this country - includes non-discrimination and gender-equality sections covering LGBT issues.

A foreign government's 2015 human-rights report on this country: documents the trial of a former ruler, police brutality, corruption, and 'discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and intersex (LGBTI) persons and other minorities'.

Stakeholder report (Oct 2015; national LGBT platform with an indigenous-peoples organisation and an international solidarity NGO) to the same UN treaty body: the March 2015 penal-code revisions (three amended provisions) added sexual-orientation protections (1 year jail or fine for discrimination), but implementation lags; government members' anti-gay positions and media/music-industry hostility perpetuate homophobia.

UN treaty-body meeting summary (July 2024): committee experts commended this country's commitment to judicial independence during its fourth ICCPR periodic-report review, asking about the national human-rights institution and indigenous rights.

National LGBT platform's pre-session summary for the UN periodic state review (March 2016): since the 2011 review, this country equalised the age of consent and added discrimination provisions (2015); but the pension act excludes same-sex couples from survivor pensions contrary to the constitution's non-discrimination principle; the platform has never been included in consultative processes.
blindLocalsOnly: The absence of legal gender recognition is resident-facing; the 2022 labour act and the harassment reports concern residents.
